corpusSummary: Annual 2026 work coalesces around (1) LLMs as research tools and methodological enablers across disciplines; (2) human–AI interaction, trust, embodiment, and ethics in everyday use; (3) AI in education and AI literacy with equity considerations; (4) health, misinformation, and governance frameworks addressing safety, bias, and cultural adequacy. The corpus also highlights policy-relevant AI adoption, design collaboration, and public-participation applications.

themes.name: LLMs as research tools and methodological enablers
themes.description: Papers show how LLMs enable new workflows, codebook generation, cross-domain analysis, and multi-agent simulations for social science and humanities research.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, embodiment, and ethics
themes.description: Studies investigate trust dynamics, perceived humanness and empathy, AI device embodiment, privacy concerns, and social implications of AI interactions.

themes.name: AI in education, literacy, and equitable access
themes.description: Research on AI tutors, classroom integration, AI literacy for diverse users, and equity considerations in learning and assessment.

themes.name: Health, governance, and ethical concerns of AI
themes.description: Work on AI’s role in health information, misinformation, patient safety, and equity-focused governance frameworks.
